Benchmark_Tables_Used: Hospital, Flights, Beers, Rayyan, Movies, Tax
Error_Definition: A cell is an error when its dirty value differs from the clean value after Raha's normalisation (unescape HTML, collapse whitespace, strip)
Split_Strategy: No split: runs on one dirty table (transductive); scored on the cells of the same table that were not labelled
Leakage_Risk: Training and evaluation instance are the same table; nothing is held out
ContextGuard_Contrast: ContextGuard scores on a held-out test split of each table (entity-aware) and on five unseen tables with 0 labels; the 20 labelled rows of B3 are excluded from scoring (Rule D8)

Error_Definition: Same cell rule as Raha; a repair counts when it equals the clean value
Split_Strategy: Transductive on the target table; reported once with perfect detection and once end to end after Raha
Leakage_Risk: Repair quality is measured on the table the labels came from
ContextGuard_Contrast: End-to-end repair (detection errors included) on held-out rows and unseen tables

Error_Definition: Violations of denial constraints, plus dictionaries and statistics
Split_Strategy: No labels and no split: probabilistic inference over the whole table instance
Supervision_Budget: 0 labels; hand-written denial constraints (9 for Hospital)
Leakage_Risk: Evaluated on the instance it cleans; constraints are written by people who know the table
ContextGuard_Contrast: B1 mines the constraints automatically (g3 dependency scan) on the test-split table, so a rule baseline exists for every table

Benchmark_Tables_Used: 12 source tables, among them Rayyan, Movies, Credit, Restaurant, Marketing, Soccer
Error_Definition: Dirty and clean versions with error-type annotations; errors generated by a LoRA-tuned Llama 3.1 8B
Split_Strategy: Releases training files (dataset/train/*.jsonl, 29,527 examples) built from all 12 tables
Leakage_Risk: Its released training files contain our unseen test tables (checked in M1), so training on them would leak
ContextGuard_Contrast: Not used for training; only the annotation files (error types) and the unseen test tables are used. Llama 3.1 licence terms are noted in the attribution table
Evidence: M1 report, Section 7.3, item on pre-packaged training triplets

Error_Definition: Error detection as a prompt-based task
Split_Strategy: Instruction tuning of 7-13B local models on its own instruction set
Leakage_Risk: Hospital was part of its training data, so its reported Hospital F1 is not an unseen-table result
ContextGuard_Contrast: Jellyfish-Instruct is not used; test tables are never touched during preparation

Benchmark_Tables_Used: Hospital, Flights, Beers, Rayyan, Billionaire, Movies, Tax
Error_Definition: Cell-level error detection by LLM reasoning
Split_Strategy: Zero-shot: no labelled training rows; open models (Qwen2.5-72B by default, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama 3.1-70B and 8B) run with vLLM; GPT-4o-mini only for cost measurements
Leakage_Risk: Public benchmark tables may appear in LLM pre-training data; the paper's handling of this was not checked, so it is an open risk for any pre-trained LLM, ours included
ContextGuard_Contrast: Billionaire is an unseen test table for ContextGuard; the base model's exposure to public tables is stated as a limitation
